messages:
maya: quick question — for rollout metadata: should pins be identity-level (namespace-scoped pin ids) or label-first (freeform labels + selectors)? trying to decide defaults and client-resolver complexity.

sanjay: namespace-scoped pins = strong invariant. a single pin id => easy eviction/transfer semantics, cheap to index, clear ownership. downside: less flexible for multi-criteria routing.

olivia: labels let us attach orthogonal signals (canary, quantized, low-latency) and compose selection rules. but client/server must evaluate selectors and we risk label explosion.

kevin: storage + lookup cost concern if we model labels as primary index. also: client resolver complexity. clients may need to compute "best-match" with multiple label weights which we don’t currently have infra for.

maya: agreed. thinking of a hybrid: canonical pin_id (global unique) for hard binding + optional labels/annotations used by routing/telemetry. pin_id drives eviction/affinity; labels drive route selection and cost heuristics.

olivia: curious how TTL and soft vs hard pins work in that model. e.g., a label that says "canary" should be easy to retire without disrupting a hard pin.

sanjay: propose semantics: pin {pin_id, namespace?}. namespace present => strong, tenant-scoped hard pin (can't be auto-evicted without explicit unpin). labels => soft hints, can be ignored by fallback. TTL applied to both but TTL on namespace/hard pins requires explicit renewal to auto-extend.

kevin: sample metadata payload idea (proto/json):
```json
{
  "pin_id": "pin_20260403_0b4f",
  "namespace": "tenant:acme",    // optional
  "labels": ["canary","cpu-q4"],
  "affinity_weight": "0.8",      // routing hint
  "expiry": "2026-05-03T00:00:00Z",
  "origin": "console",           // who created it
  "owner": "platform-team"
}
```

maya: I like that. two followups: 1) policy for conflicting pins (same namespace multiple pin_ids) and 2) whether labels should be match-exact vs prefix/tag semantics.

olivia: conflict policy: owner/creation-timestamp tie-breaker + explicit "override" flag. default: newest wins but surface an ops alert.

sanjay: for labels, recommend exact-match + boolean selectors for now (has_label X, label_in [A,B]). prefix semantics are nice but complicate index and accidental collisions. we can add more expressive selectors later.

ops-bot: (note) autoscaler: namespace-scoped pins will be treated as capacity locks. removing a namespace pin triggers scale-down checks.

kevin: one more perf thought: support an optional compact label bitmap (label_ids) for fast selection on hot-paths. compute label->id mapping in the control plane.

maya: consensus check: implement hybrid: canonical global pin_id + optional namespace for hard pins; labels as soft routing hints with exact-match selectors; TTL supported for both but namespace TTL requires manual renewal for persistence. we add override flag and tie-breaker rules.

olivia: :thumbsup: happy with that. I'll draft follow-up RFC and include selector/simple-proto.

sanjay: I'll add conflict resolution examples and a short ops playbook for pin removal.

kevin: I'll prototype the compact label-id map and a resolver spec for SDKs.

maya: thanks — next steps: olivia to RFC, kevin + sanjay to pass PRs for resolver + storage changes. leaving this thread open for inline comments.

ops-bot: Canary deploy for pin-resolution-service queued (canary id: cr-77).
